at 10 nm putting more layers on top will not pose that big of cooling problem.

All those material engineers who have been focusing on doing one thing for so long, shrinking silicon, now have to do something else. Also the prize for finding something better just go a whole lot bigger. Any new CPU inventor using novel materials and methods now does not have to worry about AMD or Intel just shrinking its transistors to compete against.

Moore's Law coming to an end does not mean performance starts to stagnate, even without a major change in technology such as graphene may provide. For instance right now there is enormous room for improvement in parallelization on the software side of things. It is a complete pain in the ass for developers to efficiently utilize arbitrary numbers of parallel processors. There have been enormous gains here lately, but it's still a very manual process. If this process could be efficiently automated, we'd suddenly be back to exponential processing gains in performance in no time.
